key_insight: The paper shows that a coherent Ising machine can accelerate Bayesian MAP inference for tokamak plasma parameter inversion by solving the posterior optimization as a spin-Hamiltonian search problem.
engineering_relevance: This offers a potential route to near-real-time fusion plasma control by replacing expensive sampling-based inversion with fast hardware-assisted optimization.
method: Formulate the negative log-posterior from multi-diagnostic Bayesian plasma inference as an Ising spin model.
Run the optimization on a coherent Ising machine using coupled DOPOs and vacuum-fluctuation-driven bifurcation dynamics.
Use a block-wise iterative decomposition to fit current qubit/oscillator limits for large-scale inference.
evidence_signal: On EAST tokamak plasma current profile inversion, the method reports a single-run solution time of about 1 ms.
watch_item: The approach is not yet fully real-time because hardware size limits require block-coordinate iteration rather than solving the full problem at once.
paper_title: Solving Large-Scale Parameter Inference in Controllable Nuclear Fusion via Coherent Ising Machines and Block Coordinate Descent
